question: Chlorine gas reacts with potassium iodide solution to form potassium chloride and iodine. This reaction is an example of a:
solution:
The correct answer is __**displacement reaction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **displacement reaction** occurs when an atom or group of **atoms in a molecule are replaced by another atom**.
 
• Metals are arranged in** descending order of their reactivities** to form a series known as the **activity series or reactivity series**.
 
• There are **two types** of displacement reaction: **single displacement reaction and double displacement reaction**.
 
• **One element is replaced by another in a compound** in a** single displacement reaction** while **double displacement reactions** happen when a portion of two ionic compounds is transferred, resulting in the** creation of two new compounds**.
 
• When chlorine gas reacts with a potassium iodide solution, **chlorine displaces iodine** to form potassium chloride and iodine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Any reaction in which **two or more chemicals combine to create a single new substance** is referred to as a **combination reaction**.
 
• The chemical reaction in which **one reactant splits into two or more products** is called a **decomposition reaction**.
 
• When **reactant ions switch positions to create new products**, the reaction is referred to as a **double displacement reaction**.
